key_insight: The paper builds a Lean 4 certification framework that can formally verify core number field invariants such as discriminants, signatures, unit-related data, and class groups.
engineering_relevance: It turns expensive algebraic number theory computations into machine-checkable proofs, enabling more trustworthy computer algebra pipelines and database validation.
method: Extend prior certified rings-of-integers work to new invariants: signature, units modulo p-th powers, and class group.
Improve discriminant certification with stronger methods for higher-degree number fields.
Use reusable Lean representations for computational ideal arithmetic plus SageMath-generated certificates and proofs.
evidence_signal: The framework was used to verify hundreds of L-functions and Modular Forms Database (LMFDB) entries for discriminant, signature, class number, and class group structure.
watch_item: The approach depends on generating reliable certificates and translating them into Lean proofs, so implementation correctness and certification coverage remain key constraints.
